claims.text: Rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys based primarily on 3d transition metals can exhibit magnetic behavior.
Short-range chemical order among Co, Ni, Fe, and Mn creates a near-critical magnetic state.
The proposed near-critical magnetic state amplifies low-field-induced spin alignment.
Amplified low-field spin alignment produces a large reversible magnetic entropy change without a first-order phase transition.
Avoiding a first-order phase transition preserves low hysteresis, rapid heat exchange, and mechanical stability.
The intended initial material is a homogeneous, single-phase, equiatomic or near-equiatomic alloy composed primarily of magnetic 3d elements.
Changing the Mn/Fe ratio adjusts local exchange interactions.
Changing the Mn/Fe ratio adjusts the degree of short-range chemical order.
Local atomic arrangement and short-range chemical order modulate magnetic exchange interactions between the constituent 3d elements.
Fine-tuning the local chemical environment changes the balance between cooperative ferromagnetic interactions and magnetic frustration.
Balancing ferromagnetic interactions and magnetic frustration establishes a near-critical magnetic state.
In the near-critical state, applied fields below 1 T can induce substantial spin reorientation and a large magnetic entropy change.
An optimized Mn/Fe ratio will enhance magnetic entropy change under low fields relative to an equiatomic baseline.
The optimized alloy will have lower magnetic hysteresis than the equiatomic baseline.
The optimized alloy will maintain mechanical integrity.
The baseline equiatomic alloy has a moderate magnetocaloric effect, higher hysteresis, and less optimal heat-exchange behavior.

The proposed behavior is limited to single-phase, well-annealed alloys with uniform microstructures, while multiphase regions or defect-dominated behavior may eliminate the magnetocaloric and mechanical advantages.
